SUMMARY

Meta Platforms, Inc.(META+0.47%)reported a total revenue increase driven by ad performance gains and sustained user engagement across its Family of Apps. Management announced the establishment of a new nonvoting Class C capital stock and a corresponding 2-for-1 stock split expected to begin trading in late Jan. 2027. The company is focusing its operational strategy on the Muse personal superintelligence platform, which achieved significant early adoption in North America. Meta is realigning Reality Labs investments to prioritize AI integration while projecting a decrease in segment losses for the upcoming fiscal year.

Operator:Good afternoon. My name is Krista, and I will be your conference operator. Today. At this time, I would like to welcome everyone to Meta's Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. All lines have been placed on mute to prevent any background noise. After the speakers' remarks, there will be a question-and-answer session. We ask that you limit yourself to 1 question. And this call will be recorded. Thank you very much. Rob, Bevagni, Meta's Director of Investor Relations, you may begin.

Mark Elliot Zuckerberg:Thank you. Good afternoon, and welcome to Meta Platform's third quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me today to discuss our results are Mark Elliot Zuckerberg, CEO and Susan J. Li, CFO. Our remarks today will include forward-looking statements, which are based on assumptions as of today. Actual results may differ materially as a result of various factors, including those set forth in today's earnings press release and in our quarterly report on Form 10 Q filed with the SEC. We undertake no obligation to update any forward-looking statement. During this call, we will present both GAAP and certain non GAAP financial measures. A reconciliation of GAAP to non GAAP measures is included in today's earnings press release.

Earnings press release and an accompanying investor presentation are available on our website at[email protected]. And now, I would like to turn the call over to Mark. Alright. Hey, everyone. Thanks for joining today. This has been a busy and exciting few months. Our Family of Apps is now used by 3.64 billion people each day, and we are seeing all time highs in engagement on both Facebook and Instagram driven by strong growth in video. Threads has now overtaken x in monthly actives and to grow quickly. WhatsApp is hitting all time highs and is becoming an increasingly important platform for agents as well.

In the last few months, we have had several major milestones towards our goal of delivering personal superintelligence to everyone. We had 1 of our most successful launches ever with the Muse personal agent, We shipped Muse Wonder as our first frontier model. We shipped several new glasses and gadgets with Muse integration including coming soon to our new audio glasses.

We have been discussing our vision for personal superintelligence for more than a year, I want to help every person have an extremely capable personal agent that understands your goals and can help you achieve them and improve your life in whatever ways you want whether that is improving your relationships, helping you save time, save money, build a business, create new things, or anything else that you can dream of. Muse is the product form of this vision. So now we have the foundational technology in place to deliver this. There is still a lot of work ahead, but our initial position is very strong.

In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the US and Canada have set up Muse personal agents, Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number 1 in the App Store almost every day. Engagement and retention are also off to a strong start, About 25% of people who have set up Muse use it on any given day. For our earliest adopters, the longer that they use Muse, the better the retention seems to get. So to put this in perspective, this is more than 2x the level that Threads started at or where we believe that other AI apps started at as well.

The most common use case for Muse is shopping. With more than 25% of people who are using Muse engaging in this with an average purchase size of over $200. Plaid told us that they had not seen activity like they are seeing with their connector on any other service before. And in the first week, we had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits since the volumes were above what any of us expected. Beyond shopping, the most common connectors are for personal productivity and connecting Muse to your other services like email and calendar.

Now this shows the importance of the Muse secure VM that we have built to provide state-of-the-art privacy and security we are looking forward to following up soon with the Muse confidential VM which will make it so that even Meta cannot see your content. We have also seen that Muse wonder improves quality engagement and retention further, which suggests that as we continue to improve intelligence, Muse will perform better and better over time. Now that Muse has clear product market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling it. The goals for this next phase play to many of Meta's strengths.

We need to do 3 things, scale the product, grow revenue, and optimize compute costs. We expect to grow Muse to serve billions of people. This is both our mission and our strategy. it is our mission in that we believe in putting the power of personal superintelligence in everyone's hands. We believe that is the path to ensuring a positive future for everyone with individual empowerment as the source of prosperity, and balance of power is the foundation for safety. On a values level, we believe that delivering this capability widely is the best thing that we can be doing.

This is also our strategy because we think that billions of muses in a network at scale will be able to get more done for people and businesses by working together. So we would like to create a large scale Muse network as quickly as possible. From a business perspective, the average revenue per American user for our existing Muse users is. Sorry. For our existing Family of Apps users is several hundreds of dollars annually, and we expect that Muse will reach an even higher level over time due to the amount of commerce that we already see taking place. This will take some time, but we are starting to work on this now.

Our business model will have a few components. For most people, the product should be free, and we will build commerce tools so we get paid a fee based on the transactions that we help facilitate. We expect this will be paid for by businesses. For people who want the most advanced models or to use extra tokens, they subscribe directly and pay. For business owners who want additional features, to use Muse to grow their businesses or for companies that want people to use Muse for work, they will be able to subscribe directly and pay as well.

And for those who want Muse to help improve the personalization and quality of their content and ads across Meta, they will be able to connect to those experiences as well. Just to clarify, the average revenue that I was talking about before is the Family of Apps revenue for our existing Muse users. On the compute side, we are building out the capacity to serve more than a billion people over the next few years. In the near term, Muse is very compute intensive to run. But we expect to improve its cost efficiency by more than 10x in the next year, which will enable it to be profitable once the revenue lines are at scale.

If compute efficiency continues improving quickly for another few years, which we think is highly likely, then Muse will be highly profitable over the years. In the near term, the strength of our core business enables us to scale the Muse network before then, and we believe that we are the best positioned company to pursue this strategy. 1 other note on compute economics is that since training is a large fixed cost, now that we have leading models, we want to serve as much high margin inference demand as possible. That is why we are building the Meta Enterprise platform led by CJ Desai.

Muse, Wonder, and even more advanced models that we are training can serve additional high margin services beyond the Muse network including our API, Muse code, and other enterprise services. A fundamental feature of our business is that we have many good uses for this compute. It is difficult to forecast the exact growth rates for the Muse network, for our enterprise platform and for how Muse wonder and beyond will accelerate our core business. But through building up multiple ways to deploy these advanced models, we increase the chances that 1 or more of them significantly outperforms our expectations.

Beyond serving other businesses, we have not yet found the limit of how effectively we can apply compute to accelerating our own core business. We have implemented an evaluation with MuseWonder to improve how effectively it can autonomously improve our recommendation and ad systems. And as our upcoming models get even more advanced, I expect that we are going to see an increasing rate of improvement in these systems. Alright. Let's talk about the models now. MuseWonder is state-of-the-art across many dimensions that matter for personal superintelligence.

This validates the importance of training models ourselves to deliver the best experience, In addition to Muse, we have also seen that engagement per person in Meta AI has more than doubled since April, when we started rolling out our new models. While Muse Wonder has been our most important release, I have been very pleased with our pace of execution here. In the last few months, we have shipped Muse Spark 1.2 and 1.3, Muse code, 2 open weights models with Muse Glimmer and Muse Spark Open, also Muse Voice.

Going forward with the field advancing quickly, we plan to focus on both pushing the frontier of intelligence and distilling those models into much smaller and more efficient product models that will be optimized for personal agents. My view is that we will be able to build super intelligence through scaling, so we are methodically working our way up the ladder there. We are already working on larger models after MuseWonder, and they are going to be very impressive and capable. We are also working on new smaller models that are coming out soon that will deliver Muse Wonder intelligence more efficiently. Moving on, our work on personal superintelligence is now also the focus of Reality Labs.

Muse is coming to Meta Glasses starting next month, and that will be an important step towards this. People already love many features of the glasses already, music, calling, capturing moments, hearing assistance, and more. But over time, we expect Muse and having your personal super intelligence with you throughout the day will be the most important part of the experience. Muse is also central to the business model for the glasses. Again, our mission and strategy are to serve everyone here.

We believe in putting the power of this technology in everyone's hands So we have priced our devices not to make a large profit on the hardware, but to build a large software and superintelligence business on top of them over time. Glasses sales continue to grow rapidly, And now with Muse, we expect that paid subscriptions will increase and that this business will begin improving meaningfully from here. I also shared at Connect that we are changing our approach to virtual reality to only ship new devices when we have major breakthroughs like we had with the Meta VR glasses this year, which, of course, are the first VR experience ever in a pair of glasses.

I continue to believe that the path to delivering holographic experience of bringing together the physical and digital worlds and everyday glasses will come through VR first. But we will pace this aspect of our investment more to focus on delivering personal superintelligence first. So with these factors combined, we expect that the P&L of Reality Labs to improve from here with operating loss coming down to approximately $15 billion next year and trending towards profitability from there. Before we conclude, wanna spend a moment on the sheer velocity that we are seeing. An important part of our approach has always been to move fast. So we can learn quickly and serve people better at scale.

But recently, things have accelerated. The last year, we shipped edits, and it has already passed 50 million actives. New apps like Forum and Seller were built by small teams and are scaling quickly to serve power users. Muse went from an idea on a whiteboard to a successful product in just about 8 months, and we are about to ship Muse Charm, which will have gone from concept to a hardware device in people's pockets in less than 1 year. I am proud of what we are building. People have all kinds of different opinions about the future.

But at Meta, we believe that the future is for everyone and that putting power in people's hands is how we get there. I think that this matters, There needs to be a company out there that represents these ideas. But this is not just about ideas. it is also about execution. So I am grateful for everyone who is working so hard to deliver all of this to billions of people around the world, And as always, thank you to everyone who is on this journey with us. And now here's Susan.

Susan J. Li:Thanks, Mark, and good afternoon, everyone. Let's begin with our consolidated segment results. All comparisons are on a year over year basis unless otherwise noted. Q3 total Family of Apps revenue was $64.2 billion, up 26%. Q3 Family of Apps ad revenue was $63.1 billion, up 26% on both the reported and constant currency basis. In Q3, the total number of ad impressions served across our services increased 10%. Impression growth was healthy across all regions, driven by growth in engagement and users, as well as ad load optimizations. The global average price per ad increased 14% year over year driven by ad performance gains and improvements in macro conditions relative to Q3 of last year.

This was partially offset by strong impression growth particularly from lower monetizing surfaces and regions. Family of apps other revenue was $1.1 billion and grew 59%. Driven primarily by WhatsApp paid messaging and subscriptions revenue. Within our Reality Labs segment, Q3 revenue was $443 million, down 6% due to lower Quest headset sales, which were partially offset by continued strong growth in AI glasses revenue. Moving now to our consolidated results. Q3 total revenue was $64.6 billion. Up 26% on both a reported and constant currency basis. Total expenses were $51.6 billion, up 68% compared to last year, an included a $9.9 billion charge related to the August 2026 multistate attorneys general agreement.

Year over year growth was primarily driven by legal related costs infrastructure costs, and third party AI token costs. The growth in infrastructure costs was driven by higher third party cloud spend depreciation, and data center operating costs. We ended Q3 with over 66 thousand employees, down 12% from Q2 following the May 2026 headcount reduction. Third quarter GAAP operating income was $13 billion, representing a 37% decline year over year and a 20% operating margin. Excluding the Q3 legal charges related to the aforementioned legal settlement, our third quarter operating income would have increased 11% year over year. Our tax rate for the quarter was 24% above our outlook range primarily driven by the nondeductible portion of legal expenses.

Net income was $9.9 billion, or $3.83 per share. Capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, were $34.9 billion, driven by investments in servers, data centers, and network infrastructure. Free cash flow was negative $2.1 billion. We ended the quarter with $82.4 billion in cash and marketable securities and $83.7 billion in debt. Turning now to the business performance. There are 2 primary factors that drive our revenue performance our ability to deliver engaging experiences for our community and our effectiveness at monetizing that engagement over time. On the first, we continue to see significant gains from our content recommendation initiatives.

On Instagram, global time spent per user reached an all time high and grew double digits year over year in Q3 with strength across both reels and feed. On Facebook, Reels time spent reached all time highs both globally and in the US, with both growing double digits year over year. Threads also continued to scale with time spent per user growing over 20% year over year. Engagement gains across our services continue to be driven by improvements we are making to the relevance, personalization, and timeliness of the content we recommend. Investments into our recommendations engine across retrieval and ranking have continued to yield positive results on Instagram and Facebook.

For instance, on Instagram Reels, our relevance launches in Q3 increased Reels time spent by over 4%. Driven in part by our upgraded model architecture that ranks sequences of reels at a time instead of evaluating each reel independently. As well as improvements we made to add richer watch time watch-time signals. On Facebook Feed and Reels, we completed the global launch of a new generative retrieval architecture, which inspired by LLMs, labels pieces of content with semantic representations and generates potential recommendations. Helping our systems surface relevant new posts before they have accumulated significant engagement.

This new architecture is now rolled out to roughly 1-quarter of unconnected feed views and half of Reels views and increased Reels watch time by 1%. Our recommendations work is also helping us deliver fresher and more personalized content. Nearly 45% of recommended Reels are now less than 1 day old, up more than 11 percentage points from Q2. On Facebook reels, we doubled the amount of history our ranking model can consider. driving a 1% increase in Reels watch time in the US. LLMs are also helping us understand content more deeply. We continue to process public Instagram posts each day through LLM based content understanding systems.

These signals have improved the engagement with Instagram search results by 1% through the end of this quarter. This quarter, we also began moving our content understanding models onto our first party Muse model family. In offline evaluations, these models are outperforming our prior production models and are reducing per unit content processing costs by more than 80% across Instagram threads, Facebook, and ads. Beyond improving quality, owning more of this stack gives us greater flexibility to develop models around the signals that matter the most for personalization. Turning to the second driver of our revenue performance. Increasing monetization efficiency. We see significant opportunity to continue improving performance for the businesses who use our services.

Within our ad systems, we are continuing to drive performance gains as we deploy more predictive models that understand users more deeply and deliver ad experiences better aligned with their unique preferences while also making our infrastructure more efficient. Last quarter, we introduced Meta Generative Recommender, which uses LLMs to reason across ad content and user preferences to predict the best ad for each person. In Q3, we launched this approach to generative retrieval on Facebook feed, driving a nearly 2% increase conversions across targeted segments. In addition, we expanded our JEM model for ads ranking to additional surfaces, driving a 1.7% increase in conversions for off-site conversion campaigns and a 9.6% increase in app ad conversions.

And we continue to scale our retrieval systems efficiently. In Q3, improvements to Andromeda such as scaling model complexity and throughput, increased conversions by 1.4%. On Facebook. We are also leveraging AI to make it easier for businesses to manage campaigns develop creative, and act on performance opportunities. Meta AI Business Assistant is becoming a more proactive and capable partner for advertisers. We estimate that advertisers who adopted its recommendations drove almost 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion and increased their advertising investment by 9% compared with similar non adopters. We are rolling out additional capabilities including creative insights, stronger business context, and more Agentic actions.

These features will allow marketers to plan, create, and optimize campaigns as well as schedule tasks and alerts through a conversational experience with approvals and previews that keep them in control. I will share 1 example of how Meta AI Business Assistant is empowering our advertisers. Simply Organic Maple, a family run maple syrup producer in Vermont, used Meta AI Business Assistant to improve its campaign messaging. After the Business Assistant recommended testing longer, more descriptive advertising copy, the business saw a 57% increase in purchases and a 36% reduction in cost per purchase. Its strongest revised ad delivered a 3x return on ad spend, a 52% improvement from the original.

Adoption of our generative AI ad creative tools also continues to scale. In Q3, nearly 10 million advertisers used at least 1 of these tools. Advertiser adoption of our video generation features grew 25% quarter over quarter, driven in part by ready made videos that reduce generation time to just a few seconds from a single image upload. Also expanding the opportunity at the intersection of creators and advertising. Partnership ads, which allow advertisers to run ads with creators, brands, and other businesses, continued to scale rapidly in Q3. Our partnership ads product grew over 97% year over year and surpassed $15 billion in annual revenue run rate.

In Q3, we also completed the global rollout creator marketing hub to all advertisers, bringing creator discovery, content and partnership ad activation into 1 place with more than 10 million creators now discoverable. We are integrating Meta AI Business Assistant into the hub so advertisers can conversationally search for creators, identify content to use in partnership ads, and get guidance across their creator marketing workflows. Outside of ads, we are also building out additional ways to monetize engagement across our ecosystem. In September, we announced the global expansion of Meta 1, our unified subscription service for consumers, creators, and businesses.

Meta 1 is rolling out gradually with more than 50 features across Facebook, and WhatsApp, including Meta Business Agent and Meta AI, and has surpassed 15 million subscriptions and trials to date. The core experience across our apps and Meta AI will remain free, while subscriptions offer more specialized capabilities and expanded AI usage. And beyond monetizing engagement across our existing services we are building new experiences and revenue streams around consumer agents. Mark highlighted the impressive early momentum with Muse. Users have found many reasons to use Muse with the top 3 categories being shopping, personal productivity, and creativity.

We are encouraged by the breadth of use cases with shopping in particular being used by over 25% of Muse weekly actives. While our near term priority is to grow adoption and expand Muse's reach, we see multiple paths to monetization beginning with subscriptions. We also see a significant opportunity to extend Muse to small businesses. Based on a recent user survey, we estimate that at least 500 million self identified small businesses use Meta's Family of Apps to reach customers and generate revenue. Muse could help these businesses acquire customers and operate more efficiently while helping people complete transactions. Over time, consumer and business agents could connect and transact directly creating opportunities around paid usage, commerce, and business services.

Alongside growth, we are focused on building sustainable unit economics. Muse's computing intensity means that expanding its user base will require significant investment, and we expect total serving costs to rise. At the same time, we expect to improve compute cost efficiency by more than 10x over the next year driven by better utilization of off peak capacity, more efficient models, and inference optimization. As revenue scales, these efficiency gains give us confidence in our ability to build a highly profitable business over time. Moving now to our financial outlook.

We expect fourth quarter 26 total revenue to be in the range of $73 billion to $76 billion Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year over year total revenue growth based on current exchange rates. Turning to the expense and CapEx outlooks. Are raising our expense outlook to incorporate the $9.9 billion charge related to legal proceedings recognized in Q3. We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175 to $179 billion. Excluding the Q3 legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.

At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18 billion to $19 billion. For 2026, we anticipate capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135 billion to $145 billion narrowed from our prior outlook of $130 billion to $145 billion. Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our fourth quarter 26 tax rate to be between 15% and 17%. Additionally, we continue to monitor active legal and regulatory matters that could significantly impact our business and financial results.

For example, we continue to see scrutiny on youth related issues in several markets, and have a number of youth related trials scheduled in the coming months in the United States. Looking beyond 2026, we are still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year. But we expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives. Our current capacity and what is scheduled to come online gives us the flexibility to allocate resources across model training, core business growth, and the development and support of new products. Our AI investments are already delivering incremental advertising revenue through stronger engagement better recommendations, and more efficient monetization.

Building on this progress, our MSL investments are creating the foundation and infrastructure needed to unlock significant new revenue opportunities and strengthen capabilities across the business. While these investments will take longer to generate returns than those in our core business, the breadth of monetization opportunities and internal efficiencies gives us confidence in their long term potential. Looking ahead, although we are not providing a full year 2027 revenue outlook, The benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.

Separately, we remain focused on improving Reality Labs profitability As Mark mentioned, we expect losses to narrow next year to around $15 billion as we reallocate investment towards other priority areas. Primarily AI. Finally, today, we announced plans to create a new class of nonvoting capital stock, which will be distributed to all existing shareholders. Through a stock dividend. For each existing share held, stockholders will receive 1 share of the new nonvoting stock. Effectively resulting in a 2-for-1 stock split. We expect trading to begin in late January 2027.

In closing, our business momentum continued in Q3 with strong execution across our core ads and engagement initiatives, And we are also excited by our progress towards bringing superintelligence to everyone. With that, Krista, let's open up the call for questions.

Operator:Thank you. We will now open the lines for a question-and-answer session. To ensure clarity. If you are streaming today's call, please mute your computer speakers. Your first question comes from the line of Brian Nowak with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Brian Nowak:Thanks for taking my questions. I have 2, 1 on Muse, 1 on Enterprise. Maybe at first, congrats on the success of Muse. But as you analyze the user behavior and the product, can you talk with us a little bit about any of the constraints to the slope of forward user growth that you are most focused on addressing, whether it is capabilities, model efficiency, capacity, etcetera, just so we understand what are the limiting factors to forward user growth that you wanna address. And the second 1 is on enterprise.

Mark, can you just sort of walk us through your vision, for the meta Enterprise product offering and the key value drivers you hope to provide for the enterprise adopting the service?

Mark Elliot Zuckerberg:Yeah. I think I can talk about both of those, and then Susan can jump in with anything else. Alright. So right now for Muse, we are 1 of the things I pointed out is we have more than 10 million people in the US and Canada who have set it up. But I think 1 of the biggest constraints so far is that because this is a compute intensive service to run, we have not launched it globally yet. that is partially because of wanting to optimize it for each place, and there is some work around connectors for that. But it is it is partially that we wanna make sure that we do this efficiently.

So, I mean, there is pros and cons there. The pro, of course, is that just makes it even more impressive that you have 10 million people using it and signing up to use it in the first 6 weeks because those are all kind of Americans and Canadians in a small number of markets. So if we actually did roll it out more broadly, you would expect that number to be significantly larger than what we are seeing today. But then on the flip side, we actually have to go do the work to bring the efficiency in line to make that make sense.

And so that. that is that is a big part of it that we need to do. We. The compute efficiency work is going to be important. On this also because you know, we wanna make sure that we have built enough compute to be able to serve what we think is going to be a billion plus people. If we can achieve certain compute efficiency targets, but we obviously have a lot of work to do there as well. And that will be that will be 1 of the limiting factors over the next year. We wanna build out the business around it. So, I mean, I talked about that.

And I think doing that in tandem with bringing down the compute or increasing the compute efficiency is going to be important for getting this to work from a business perspective. Which I am optimistic about. But I think that is 1 of the things that we need to do. And then there is just continuing to increase the value in the product. Which I think we will largely do by continuing to develop new models that is why I mentioned that you know, we launched Muse first on Muse Spark. And that is what is currently the default across the free tier. We rolled out Muse Wonder and people can access that in the in the paid tier today.

And we know that it performs a lot better, so we are working on getting a more efficient version of Muse. Wonder that we will be able to roll out more broadly, but you can imagine just as we iterate forward and, you know, 2, 3 models into the future when you have significantly higher intelligence and capability to solve many more problems for people and the ability to deliver that at a much more affordable price point, think that is going to just unlock a lot more value to people. So we are we are very excited about that.

Transitioning to talking about the enterprise piece, because I think of these 2 pieces, there is some connection here in that you know, the main enterprise offering in the near term is going to be the model API and Muse code, and we have business agents that we have been scaling for a while. And each of those 3 things is growing quite quickly. So we are excited about that. Over time, we would like to make it so that we have a whole kind of business network of Muse agents as well. there is the business agent, which we have talked about on previous earnings calls for businesses to help out with sales and customer support.

But what we see is a lot of activity. A lot of people are actually using Muse today to help run especially small businesses. And we think that there is both an opportunity to help create an agent that people use to really enable them to automate and do a lot of the parts of spinning up a small business that are just kind of difficult and time consuming, but are not the core thing that a person is trying to do. So we think that is a big deal. And then making a version of Muse that people can bring into different corporate environments and work there, we think is gonna be a big deal.

And then beyond that, building what I refer to as the Muse network, which is making it so that Muse is not just a kind of single player game. Where you have your Muse, but making it so that your Muses can work with your friends and your families. And if you wanna buy something, it is not just navigating to that business's website. it is talking to their agent. I think that getting that all to work well together is going to unlock tremendous value at scale. So I. I am I am very excited about all of that.

I think the enterprise use is gonna be a big part of it, but it is also going to kind of have this very valuable boost in the utility for consumers too. So I am I am very excited about both of those.

Susan J. Li:I would add on to Mark's comments on enterprise. AI is creating huge amounts of disruption in enterprise today. And, you know, we do not. What we can see, we really do not believe that traditional enterprise companies have this lockdown. And in fact, you know, some of the leading companies in this space today did not exist a few years ago. Those companies made large investments in model development and we have done the same. And we have increasingly competitive models to bring to bear for the benefit of all of our users, including small businesses and including enterprises, And already today, we have 500 million businesses, using our products.

So we really believe that AI is going to reshape how businesses operate. We expect that businesses of all sizes are going to use AI agents across software development and productivity, sales, marketing, and customer service, etcetera. We have differentiated assets to serve this market, bringing together models, infrastructure, global distribution, and long standing relationships with businesses. And it is our hope that this will be able to be a new diversified recurring revenue stream for us that will be able to support multiple business models, including subscriptions and usage based API and messaging and other revenue lines.

So we expect that this will be an opportunity that will develop over multiple years, and we intend to scale our investment behind demonstrated customer demand and product market fit in this area.

Operator:Your next question comes from the line of Eric Sheridan with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Eric Sheridan:Thanks so much for taking the questions. Maybe just the first 1 building on Brian's question. When you think about the friction points around Agentic commerce, how do you guys as a company think about solving for friction that is rising where there are aggregators or suppliers that do not want agents to interact with their platforms or their services, and how you think about lowering that friction or creating the right balance between the existing services that consumers access today relative to how this might all be changed or altered by Agentic behavior over the medium to long term.

And the second 1 would be with the announcement of the new class of shares tonight with earnings, any updated thoughts broadly about how you think about sources of capital and optimizing your capital structure to make sure you invest the proper amounts to capitalize on the opportunities that AI presenting in the next couple of years. Thanks so much.

Mark Elliot Zuckerberg:I can answer the first 1. So, okay. So the question-- what. sorry. What was the what was the first question there? Friction points around Agentic commerce. Got it. Alright. Yeah. So the right now, what we are seeing is that overwhelmingly, businesses are very excited about enabling this because they recognize that it is going to be a new opportunity for them not only to increase the sales and the quality of the experience for existing customers, but potentially to bring in new customers. So now, I mean, across the whole business ecosystem, different people will kind of adopt this at different paces.

And how our strategy evolves on that to develop the ecosystem will depend on how that goes. But overall, I would say we have been very positively surprised by how quickly I think a huge amount of businesses have wanted to know, not only figure out how to make it so that Muse can use their services more effectively, but have reached out to us to integrate around it. So I view that as a very good sign. And, you know, obviously, everyone wants to be an early adopter. that is fine. We will we will we will work with folks on the terms that makes sense for them.

But I do think that over time, this is gonna be quite valuable for everyone to make this work well, and I think we are on a good trajectory on that so far.

Susan J. Li:Yeah. I would add to that, and I will also answer your second question and just say, you know, I think agents are going to be an important part of you know, how reality evolves, and I think everyone is going to have to adapt to what that means, the new age of Agentic commerce.
